preamble: Debuccalization of a rhotic to the glottal stop [ʔ]. In Late Egyptian, /r/ (together with /t/ and /j/) became /ʔ/ at the end of a stressed syllable and was eventually lost word-finally; this is why Egyptian ḥr 'face' is reconstructed as Classical Coptic /hoʔ/. The Kuki-Chin cases go through an intermediate velar stop and belong in r_to_k and k_to_glottal_stop.

examples.note: The coda r of the stressed syllable became a glottal stop, which Classical Coptic reconstructions keep as /ʔ/.
